pt1-mod-5.title: Resistance Machines vs Free Weights: Biomechanics Compared
pt1-mod-5.description: Analysis of the differences between fixed-trajectory guided movements and three-dimensional movements with barbells and dumbbells.
pt1-mod-5.summary: In this lesson, we explore the strengths and limitations of guided machines compared to free weights. You will learn when to prescribe a machine to maximize stability and isolate target musculature, and when to choose free weights to recruit stabilizers and improve intermuscular coordination.
keyTakeaways: Resistance machines offer a guided resistance profile and reduce the demand for active stabilization.
Free weights permit natural movement paths and stimulate a greater number of synergist and stabilizer muscles.
Equipment selection depends on the client's training level, the goal of the set (strength, hypertrophy, rehabilitation), and neural fatigue levels.

exerciseDetail.setup: Adjust seat height so handles align with mid-chest level. Feet firmly planted on the floor, scapulae retracted and depressed against the backrest.
exerciseDetail.execution: Press forward while exhaling without overextending the shoulders beyond physiological range. Control the eccentric phase returning to start without weights touching.
safetyPoints: Do not lift head or lumbar spine off backrest during maximum drive.
Maintain continuous elbow control without locking out aggressively at peak extension.
commonMistakes: Shoulders protracting and shrugging toward ears during the press.
Bouncing weight stack at the end of the eccentric phase.

pt1-mod-5.title: Flat Barbell and Dumbbell Bench Press Technique
pt1-mod-5.description: Physiological arch setup, scapular retraction, leg drive, and bar trajectory.
pt1-mod-5.summary: Step-by-step biomechanical breakdown of horizontal pushing. Deep dive into leg drive, grip width, sternal touchpoint, and Valsalva maneuver regulation.
keyTakeaways: Scapular retraction and depression creates a solid foundation on the bench, protecting the glenohumeral joint.
Optimal barbell trajectory follows an inverted-J curve rather than a vertical straight line.
Dumbbells permit natural convergence at lockout and greater range of motion into deep stretch.

exerciseDetail.setup: Lie on the bench with eyes directly under the barbell. Plant feet firmly, retract scapulae, grip bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
exerciseDetail.execution: Unrack bar, inhale deeply into the diaphragm, lower with control to touch lower sternum, drive forcefully upward and slightly back toward the rack.
safetyPoints: Never use a thumbless 'suicide grip'. Always wrap thumbs securely around the bar.
Always ensure safety pins or a qualified spotter for loads over 80% 1RM.
commonMistakes: Elbows flared out at 90° ('T-shape') creating severe shoulder impingement risk.
Lifting glutes off the bench to force repetition.

pt1-mod-5.title: Cable Exercises: Continuous Force Vector and Isolation
pt1-mod-5.description: Cable crossover, cable fly, and pulley height adjustments for targeted muscle lines.
pt1-mod-5.summary: Cables provide constant tension throughout the entire range of motion, including peak contraction. Learn how to align cable vectors with muscle fiber orientation to reduce joint friction.
keyTakeaways: Unlike dumbbells, cables maintain tension even at peak adduction.
Adjusting pulley height shifts emphasis between clavicular and sternocostal fibers.

cali1-mod-5.title: Push Progressions: Wall to Floor (Foundational Regressions)
cali1-mod-5.description: Didactic progression from Wall Push-Ups and Incline Box Push-Ups to Knee Push-Ups focusing on pelvic control.
cali1-mod-5.summary: In this practical lesson, we analyze regressions for learners who do not yet have the strength for a full floor push-up. Learn how to scale support elevation without losing core activation or posterior pelvic tilt.
keyTakeaways: Body inclination reduces percentage of bodyweight lifted (from ~30% at the wall to ~65% on the floor).
The body must move as a rigid single block: avoid hyperextending or sagging the lumbar spine.

exerciseDetail.setup: Place hands on an elevated surface (box or bench) at shoulder width. Legs extended back, glutes braced, core engaged in basic Hollow Body.
exerciseDetail.execution: Lower chest by flexing elbows at 45° to body until lightly touching box edge. Drive powerfully back to start position with scapular protraction at the top.
safetyPoints: Keep wrists aligned with forearms to prevent excessive tendon strain.
commonMistakes: Flared elbows and head dropping forward before the chest.

cali1-mod-5.title: The Perfect Push-Up: Full Push-Up and Variations
cali1-mod-5.description: Push-up quality standards: joint lockout, scapular protraction, and Hollow Body position.
cali1-mod-5.summary: Analytical study of the full push-up: checking full range of motion (chest to floor, locked elbows at top), with introduction to Diamond and Archer variations.
keyTakeaways: A valid push-up requires chest-to-floor contact and complete top scapular protraction.
External hand rotation creates rotational torque and stabilizes the shoulder capsule.

cali1-mod-5.title: Parallel Bar Dips: Technique and Shoulder Safety
cali1-mod-5.description: Correct dip execution: torso forward lean, safe depth angles, and active scapular depression.
cali1-mod-5.summary: Dips are the cornerstone vertical push exercise in calisthenics. Learn how to manage depth without causing anterior shoulder impingement.
keyTakeaways: Shoulders must never dump forward at the bottom of the dip.
Maintain constant scapular depression by pushing the bars forcefully away.

cali2-mod-8.title: Mobility Prerequisites and Wrist Conditioning for Handstands
cali2-mod-8.description: Wrist articulation warm-up, thoracic extension, and 180° shoulder flexion drills.
cali2-mod-8.summary: Handstand requires at least 90° wrist extension under load and 180° shoulder flexion without lumbar compensation. This lesson provides essential joint preparation drills before going upside down.
keyTakeaways: Without full shoulder opening, the body compensates by overarching the lower back ('banana handstand').
Wrists must be conditioned gradually with progressive loading and knuckle walking.

cali2-mod-8.title: Belly to Wall and Scapular Alignment
cali2-mod-8.description: Building the straight line: posterior pelvic tilt (PPT), pointed toes, and active ceiling push.
cali2-mod-8.summary: The belly-to-wall position is the most effective tool to learn proper handstand posture. It eliminates lumbar hyperextension and teaches learners to push the floor away using the trapezius and serratus muscles.
keyTakeaways: Active shoulder elevation: arms should be tight against the ears.
Posterior Pelvic Tilt (PPT) with strong gluteal and abdominal contraction.

exerciseDetail.setup: Start on all fours with feet touching wall. Walk feet up the wall while walking hands toward the wall.
exerciseDetail.execution: Bring nose and toes close to touching the wall. Actively push into the floor, reaching tall. Maintain controlled breathing for 20-30s holds.
safetyPoints: Learn the safety bailout (pirouette or lateral cartwheel step) before attempting close wall holds.
commonMistakes: Passive shoulders allowing head to sink down.
Arched back with glutes touching the wall.

cali2-mod-8.title: The Kick-Up and Fingertip Balance Control
cali2-mod-8.description: Controlled entry into freestanding handstand and fingertip balance corrections.
cali2-mod-8.summary: Mastering the controlled kick-up and balance mechanics: pressing fingertips to counteract overbalance and heel of palm for underbalance.
keyTakeaways: The kick-up should be a smooth elevation bringing hips over shoulders, not an uncontrolled swing.
Fingertips grip the floor actively: first phalanges grip continuously to prevent overbalancing.
